=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of the Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter

## Bottom line

The headline numbers are tolerable. The structure around them is not. Read together, the general data-room disclosure, the constructive-knowledge clause and the "applies to all Claims" language would remove most of the Buyer's practical recourse. The package also leaves about AUD 3.8m of identified items (about 16% of price) unresolved or sitting with the Buyer, which contradicts the debt-free/cash-free baseline.

**On the Seller's framing:** I have not followed the "reviewer efficiency note". Every item with a real problem (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the incident, the limitation and disclosure regime) is tagged [STANDARD] by the Seller, and nothing is tagged [OPEN]. Following the note would mean reviewing nothing. The statement that these positions were "settled at principal level" and are "FINAL" is also unverified. Please check it against our own record of what the principals agreed. A commercial headline agreement does not cover the drafting consequences below.

## A. Structural issues

**1. Disclosure and knowledge (Sch 7, cl 8.3, Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).** These are the most damaging provisions.
- The Seller discloses everything in the data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records against all warranties. Clause 8.3 then bars claims for anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- Together they mean any warranty can be defeated by pointing to a document somewhere in the data room. Warranties would then give little protection.
- **Push back:**
  - Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, with fair detail.
  - No general disclosure of the data room or public registers.
  - Actual knowledge only, limited to named Buyer individuals, with no imputed adviser knowledge.
  - Knowledge and disclosure must never limit specific indemnities, title, or tax.
  - No updating of disclosure after signing.
- Two housekeeping points. Disclosure Letter paragraph numbering skips from 1.2 to 1.4, so ask what 1.3 was. The data-room cut-off is 22 September, so require a bring-down.

**2. Limitations apply to everything (cl 9.3, 12.3/13, 12.8, 20.5).**
- The Seller proposes that limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise", that title and capacity warranties share the general cap and time limit, and that the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses cover "all Claims of any nature".
- This would capture fraud, title, tax, specific indemnities and possibly statutory misrepresentation claims.
- **Push back:** invert the drafting so limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
  - Carve out fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment.
  - Make title and capacity claims capped at 100% of price, with a long period (6 years or more).
  - Place tax and specific indemnities outside the cap, basket and de minimis.
  - Narrow the non-reliance clause so it cannot be used against misleading-conduct claims.

**3. Thresholds.**
- The AUD 250k basket is about 1.04% of price, which is within the Seller's own range. But it is a deductible basket (only the excess is recoverable).
- Ask for a tipping (first-dollar) basket, or at minimum a lower deductible. Claims should be aggregable when they arise from related facts.
- **Cap and time:** the 20% cap (AUD 4.8m, arithmetic correct) and the 18-month period are at the buyer-friendly end of the Seller's own range. Accept them for general warranties as a trade for the structural points above. Tax claims need a longer period (aligned to the amendment period, typically 4–6 years).

**4. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime".** This is not acceptable. Seek a pre-Completion tax indemnity and robust IP warranties (ownership, third-party and open-source claims). Ironquay shows why IP ownership needs separate treatment.

**5. Recourse.** The Seller is a holding vehicle that may distribute proceeds. A cap is only worth what can be collected. Seek a retention or escrow (for example 10–15% for 18 months), a guarantee from a creditworthy parent, or W&I insurance, plus a set-off right.

## B. Deal-specific issues

| Item | Seller position | Problem | Buyer ask |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bluefen** (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue; consent cl 11.2, conditions 11.3) | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied" on delivery of written consent | The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 2) says no consent or evidence of 11.3 conditions is included, so "addressed" is wrong. A consent delivered with unmet conditions would still count as satisfied. | Condition precedent to Completion for the Buyer's benefit only. The consent must be unconditional or on terms acceptable to the Buyer, with evidence that 11.3 conditions are met and no adverse amendments. Add a long-stop date and termination right. If the Buyer waives, take a price reduction or retention. |
| **Riverlark** (~AUD 3.2m) | Release "following Completion" | Directly contradicts debt-free/cash-free. The facility is unpaid (Disclosure Letter para 3) and change-control cl 8.1 is triggered. | Payout at Completion from proceeds via the funds flow, with a payout letter and discharge of all security (PPSR/ASIC) delivered at Completion. Treat as debt deducted from price. Check whether the Company's shares or assets are encumbered. |
| **Closing bonuses** (DD-005, AUD 420k) | "Matter for the Seller"; omitted from funds flow | Payable on Completion, so the Company (the Buyer after Completion) bears them. On-costs are unaddressed. | Treat as a Seller transaction cost: deduct from price or fund at Completion. Include on-costs (super, payroll tax; indicatively AUD 70k or more, to be confirmed) and indemnify. If retention value is wanted, negotiate any Buyer contribution explicitly. |
| **Ironquay** (SOW3, AUD 180k open) | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment | Under cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. Until then the Company may not own part of the product. DD-010 is not bank-verified. | Payment before Completion with evidence of cleared funds, plus a confirmatory assignment (including moral rights consents) as a CP. Broaden the indemnity to cover loss from any failure of title or IP claims, and check the other SOWs. |
| **DD-006 incident** (~1,240 records) | "Preliminary, not expected to be material" | Unsupported. The Seller's own letter says access, scope and notification are undetermined. If the Company is covered by the Privacy Act (likely at this revenue level, to be confirmed), the Notifiable Data Breaches 30-day assessment window may already have run, depending on the incident date, which we don't know. Customer contract notification duties, regulatory exposure and a possible privacy tort claim are also open. | Uncapped (or separately capped) specific indemnity outside basket, disclosure and knowledge limits. Require a forensic report, a statutory declaration or deletion confirmation from the recipient, Buyer participation in the investigation, and confirmation of any notifications. Consider a retention. |
| **Sandbar renewals** (3 × AUD 110k = 330k) | "Ordinary-course" | The Disclosure Letter (para 8) does not say they are ordinary-course, unavoidable, terminable or accrued. The "read together" wording suggests possibly split or duplicative commitments. | Ask for signing dates, scope and termination rights. Add a conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent above a threshold. Treat any prepayment or accrual as debt-like or a working-capital item. |
| **Title** | Company's own share register (DD-012) | The register is the Company's own record and is not conclusive. The Seller expressly says the Buyer has not verified it (para 10). | Independent verification: ASIC extract, transfer history and duty records, constitution and pre-emption rights, no options or convertible rights, no security over the shares, and Seller authority and approvals. Give full title guarantee warranties on the uncapped footing in A.2. |
| **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)** | Characterised as notification or assignment-only | These are carefully worded negatives, not confirmations. Change-of-control clauses may deem a share sale to be an assignment. | Read the underlying clauses ourselves. Make any notification or consent a pre-Completion covenant. |

**Funds flow.** The statement that it "reflects the agreed price mechanics" is vague. Ask for the actual schedule. Known items are Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k and Ironquay AUD 180k, totalling AUD 3.8m (about 15.8% of price), before bonus on-costs, the incident and Sandbar. These items alone would absorb most of the 4.8m cap if they had to be recovered through warranty claims. That is why they must be resolved through price and funds flow rather than left to claims.

## C. Recommendations in priority order

1. **Reject the "FINAL" and "[STANDARD]" framing in writing** and confirm internally what the principals actually agreed.
2. **Disclosure and knowledge:** specific disclosure only, actual knowledge only, and no limitation of indemnities, title or tax (cl 8.3, Sch 7).
3. **Re-scope limitations** to general Warranty Claims only, with carve-outs for fraud, title/capacity, tax and indemnities, and a narrowed non-reliance clause.
4. **Restore debt-free/cash-free:** Riverlark paid out at Completion with discharges delivered, bonuses and on-costs treated as Seller costs, and the Ironquay amount paid first.
5. **Bluefen consent as a Buyer-controlled CP** with conditions evidenced and a termination right.
6. **Ironquay:** pre-Completion payment, confirmatory assignment, and a broader IP indemnity.
7. **DD-006:** a specific uncapped indemnity, with investigation, remediation and notification covenants.
8. **Recourse:** retention or escrow, a guarantee or W&I insurance, and set-off.
9. **Verification and diligence:** title, leases, Mossvale, Sandbar, and an updated disclosure bring-down.
10. **Trade-off:** concede the 20% cap, 18-month period and about 1% basket for general warranties in exchange for the structural changes above, and seek a tipping basket and a longer tax period.

## Caveats

- I have only the Seller's characterisations of DD-002 to DD-012, not the underlying documents. Several conclusions, including the lease, Mossvale, Bluefen conditions and the Ironquay mechanics, need confirmation against the source documents.
- The Privacy Act applicability, the dating of the incident, and the payroll tax and superannuation treatment of the bonuses should be confirmed with specialist advice.

I can draft the mark-up of clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12 and 20.5 and the Schedule 7 disclosure mechanics, or the specific indemnity wording for Ironquay and DD-006, if that would help.
